posts.title: Two Days Ahead: Why We Ask
posts.excerpt: We ask for two days' notice on whole celebration cakes so that our bakers can prepare every sponge, curd, and cream without compromise.
posts.content:
At our counter on Quarry Lane, people often ask why we require a full two days' notice for a whole cake. In an era when instant gratification and same-day delivery are taken for granted, forty-eight hours can feel like an unusual request for a simple dessert. Yet when you step behind the counter into our kitchen and watch how Tomasz Nowak and Mara Lindqvist work at the white-marble bench, the reason becomes clear. A cake made properly cannot be hurried, frozen in bulk, or thrown together from premade pastes.

When we opened Yoake Patisserie in 2017, we initially attempted to accommodate last-minute orders, baking extra cakes each morning and hoping they would match whatever flavours customers requested. By 2023, however, we realized that this approach compromised both our ingredients and our bakers. We made a deliberate choice to shift all whole-cake orders to a strict two-day notice window, with orders closing at 11:00 two days prior to collection. That single decision transformed the quality of our cakes and restored calm to our morning routine.

A proper celebratory cake begins long before the oven door closes. On the first day after receiving your order, Tomasz plans the bake. He weighs whole eggs, organic flour, and cultured butter, infusing syrups and steeping natural aromatics. If you have selected our lemon and almond cake, lemons must be zested and simmered slowly into citrus curd. If your choice is dark chocolate and hazelnut, hazelnuts are carefully toasted, peeled, and crushed into praline, while chocolate ganache is emulsified and left to stabilize at room temperature overnight.

The sponge itself requires proper resting. A freshly baked sponge is tender, fragile, and prone to tearing if sliced immediately. Allowing it to rest overnight at a controlled temperature relaxes the crumb, locking in moisture and ensuring it can support delicate fillings without collapsing. On the morning of your collection, Tomasz trims the sponge into even layers on our marble turntable, brushing each layer with fragrant soaking syrup and smoothing on chilled creams.

Every cake is assembled fresh on the day of collection. Whether you choose strawberry and vanilla, apricot and pistachio, or coffee and walnut, your cake is never pulled from a commercial freezer. It is finished with a smooth palette knife, decorated with natural elements, and boxed in plain white cardboard tied with pale ribbon. If you requested a message—piped by hand in chocolate up to twenty characters—it is inscribed right before the box is closed.

Collection opens at 11:00 and runs until 17:00, Wednesday through Sunday. Whether it is our 15 cm cake serving six guests for €38 or our 18 cm cake serving eight to ten for €52, each cake represents two days of quiet craftsmanship. We ask for forty-eight hours not to be difficult, but because we believe a celebration cake should be the finest thing on your table.
